channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kazakhstan Needs to Hear Civil Society, Avoid Ruining Statistics
item.description: An article titled "Don't Ruin the Statistics: Why Kazakhstan Needs to Hear Civil Society" suggests that the government should listen to its citizens. The piece implies that ignoring civil society could lead to skewed or misleading statistical data, potentially masking underlying issues within the country.

item.title: Tajikistan's Foreign Minister Addresses UN General Assembly on Peace and Water
item.description: Tajikistan's Foreign Minister Sirojiddin Mukhriddin spoke at the UN General Assembly, emphasizing peace, multilateral cooperation, and the UN's central role. He announced Tajikistan's initiative for a "Decade of Peace" (2027-2036) and highlighted the upcoming UN Water Conference in Dushanbe in 2028.

item.title: Kazakhstan sees surge in electric and hybrid vehicle sales
item.description: Sales of New Energy Vehicles (NEVs) in Kazakhstan increased by 207.4% year-on-year from January to August 2026, with 6,003 units sold. Plug-in hybrids and extended-range electric cars accounted for 72.5% of the market, with BYD leading sales.

item.title: Kazakh banks continue to lower deposit interest rates
item.description: Average interest rates on individual deposits in Kazakhstan's national currency fell to 14.6% in August, the lowest in nearly a year. Rates for corporate deposits also decreased to 15.7%. The National Bank's reduction of the base rate is expected to further lower deposit yields.

item.title: Qarmet modernizes mines and digitizes miner safety control systems
item.description: Qarmet has begun exporting coal concentrate for the first time in a long period, with nearly 500,000 tons shipped to China, India, and Russia. The company plans to increase the capacity of its "Vostochnaya" enrichment plant from 2.8 million to 4 million tons by 2030. A new control center monitors all eight major mines in real-time, enhancing worker safety.

item.title: Bishkek court reclassifies charges in '75 Letters' case, lawyer explains
item.description: Lawyers for the accused in Bishkek's "75 Letters" case have received the full court ruling. The charges were reclassified from "obstruction of citizens' electoral rights" under Article 326 to Article 195. This reclassification avoids a prison sentence, as Article 326 is considered a particularly serious crime. The Supreme Court may further reduce the sentence.

item.title: New industrial, transport, and social facilities launched across Kazakhstan regions
item.description: In line with the President's directives, Kazakhstan is developing industrial potential and modernizing infrastructure. New facilities include a corn processing plant in the Zhambyl region, an automated sorting complex in Pavlodar, and modernized railway stations in the Ulytau region. These projects aim to improve living standards and economic capacity.

item.title: Correctional facility employee sentenced for aiding inmate in West Kazakhstan
item.description: A correctional facility employee in the West Kazakhstan region has been sentenced to two years of restricted freedom for abuse of official powers. The employee illegally smuggled 100 packs of cigarettes to an inmate for 60,000 tenge and was aware of the inmate's illegal use of a mobile phone. He was also stripped of his special rank.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Anti-Corruption Agency Uncovers Online Casino Scheme
item.description: Kazakhstan's Agency for Financial Monitoring (AFM) has exposed an online casino operation in Karaganda. The scheme, active since January 2026, allegedly processed over 415 million tenge through 23 drop accounts. Two suspects are under house arrest, and their assets have been seized.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Adjust Interest Rates on Certain Foreign Currency Deposits from October 1
item.description: Starting October 1, Kazakhstan will see changes in terms for some foreign currency deposits. Banks may offer higher interest rates on long-term savings deposits denominated in foreign currencies, according to Stan.kz.

item.title: Seismologists Predict Low Probability of Major Earthquakes in Almaty
item.description: Following two seismic events today, Almaty's emergency department released information on the likelihood of future earthquakes. The National Scientific Center for Seismological Observations and Research predicts no major quakes are expected at this time. Residents are urged to remain calm and trust official data.

item.title: South Korean President's Office Demands Apology from Ukraine
item.description: The South Korean president's office has demanded an apology from Ukraine. This demand stems from reports that North Korean prisoners of war were handed over to Seoul, causing a dispute between the two nations.

item.title: Death Penalty Proposed in Uzbekistan After 5-Year-Old Girl's Rape
item.description: Uzbekistan is considering harsher penalties for sexual assault against minors following a case in Namangan region where a 5-year-old girl was raped. Saida Mirziyoyeva suggested reinstating the death penalty for such crimes, stating current laws are insufficient.

item.title: Maximum interest rates for foreign currency deposits to increase from October 1
item.description: The Kazakhstan Deposit Insurance Fund (KDIF) will raise the maximum interest rates for foreign currency savings deposits with terms exceeding 12 months to 2.5% annually, effective October 1. This change applies to new or renewed deposits after this date. Banks retain the discretion to set their own rates.

item.title: Pakistan Rejects Taliban Claims of Involvement in Afghan Border Clashes
item.description: Pakistan's Ministry of Information and Broadcasting has denied Taliban allegations of Pakistani involvement in clashes in Afghanistan's Nuristan and Kunar provinces. The ministry called the claims baseless and described circulating videos as false narratives intended to portray domestic opposition as foreign-backed.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Tourism Sector: Foreign Spending Reaches 1.8 Trillion Tenge in 2025
item.description: Foreign visitors spent 1.8 trillion tenge on trips within Kazakhstan in 2025, an increase of 29.6% year-on-year, according to the WTTC. Domestic tourism spending reached 1 trillion tenge. Tourists from Uzbekistan, Russia, and Kyrgyzstan were the most frequent visitors.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Health Reports Decrease in Medicine Prices
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Health announced a reduction in medicine prices due to revised state price regulation rules. The ministry reported that maximum prices for 3,801 drug items (76% of the list) decreased by an average of 26.5% in 2025. Prices for 947 drugs remained unchanged, while 246 new items were added.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's alcohol imports surge by 63.2 percent in seven months
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's trade deficit in the alcohol sector widened to $22.7 million in the first seven months of 2026. Imports of foreign spirits increased by 63.2 percent to $11.1 million, while domestic exports fell significantly. Russia was a major supplier, with imports from there rising 76.7 percent.

item.title: Kazakhstan to raise maximum interest rates on foreign currency deposits
item.description: Kazakhstan will increase the maximum annual interest rate on foreign currency savings deposits held for over 12 months from 1% to 2.5%. The new rates apply to deposits opened or extended after October 1. The Kazakhstan Deposit Insurance Fund announced the change.

item.title: President demands military reform plan within 10 days after soldier deaths
item.description: Following the deaths of 14 servicemen during exercises, the President has sharply criticized the military leadership for "criminal unprofessionalism." He demanded a concrete, phased military reform plan within 10 days from the Security Council and the Ministry of Defense, citing irresponsibility and negligence.

item.title: State auto base returned to government ownership in Aytmatov district
item.description: The prosecutor's office in Aytmatov district has recovered a state auto base and a 4.7-hectare land plot valued at 94 million soms. The property was illegally transferred to private ownership in 2005 and used by private individuals. The prosecutor's office took measures to return the assets to state control.

item.title: Supreme Audit Chamber finds unjustified expenses in ministry travel and procurement
item.description: The Supreme Audit Chamber has identified unjustified expenses within ministries. The Ministry of Industry could not confirm a portion of its 139.5 million tenge procurements. The Ministry of Trade overstated its foreign travel expenses by 15.5 million tenge, according to Stan.kz.

item.title: Tajikistan and Gabon establish diplomatic relations at UN Headquarters
item.description: Tajikistan's Foreign Minister Sirojiddin Mukhriddin and Gabon's Foreign Minister Marie-Edith Tasilla-Yé-Dombéni signed an agreement establishing diplomatic relations between the two countries. The meeting took place on September 24, 2026, in New York during the 81st UN General Assembly session.

item.title: Passenger Dies in Bishkek E-Bike Accident, Driver Arrested
item.description: A passenger on an electric bicycle died after being hit by a car in Bishkek on September 27. The driver of the Mazda 323, suspected of being intoxicated, was detained. A criminal case has been initiated.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Participates in CSTO Military Exercises in Russia
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is participating in the CSTO military exercises 'Interaction-2026', 'Search-2026', and 'Echelon-2026' held at the Chebarkulsky training ground in Russia. The exercises involve contingents from Kyrgyzstan, Belarus, Kazakhstan, Russia, and Tajikistan.

item.title: Central Asian customs agencies to enhance data exchange and risk management
item.description: Customs authorities from Kazakhstan, China, Kyrgyzstan, and Uzbekistan agreed on a draft procedure for operational data exchange. The document, to be signed at the 3rd China-Central Asia summit in 2027, aims to accelerate cargo movement, improve customs control accuracy, and increase trade route transparency. Discussions also covered AI and big data in customs risk management.

item.title: Kazakhstan's exports to Turkey surge, driven by coal and engines
item.description: Kazakhstan's trade with Turkey reached $4.7 billion in January-July 2026, a 1.6-fold increase. Exports grew significantly in coal, oil products, and copper. While exports of polymers and cotton fiber decreased, imports also declined, notably in clothing and confectionery.

item.title: Iran ready for 'apocalyptic war' if provoked, says Foreign Minister
item.description: Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi stated that while he and President Masoud Pezeshkian came to New York with a message of peace, Iran is prepared for an 'apocalyptic war' if provoked. He reiterated Iran's steadfastness against any aggression and readiness for 'real diplomacy'.

item.title: Tajikistan inaugurates new solar, wind, and hydro power facilities in Gorno-Badakhshan
item.description: President Emomali Rahmon commissioned new energy facilities in Tajikistan's Gorno-Badakhshan Autonomous Province on September 27. These include a 110/35 kV substation in Ishkashim, a 3 MW solar power station in Shughnan, a 112 kW solar station in Rushan, and a 25 kW small hydropower plant in Bartang.

item.title: US-Iran indirect talks resume today with Qatari mediation, media reports
item.description: A new round of indirect negotiations between the United States and Iran is scheduled to take place today, according to Axios, citing sources. Mediators from Qatar will hold separate meetings with Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi and US Special Envoy Steve Witkoff.

item.title: China ready to work with all nations for historical multilateralism and shared development
item.description: China is prepared to collaborate with all countries to preserve historical multilateralism and promote global development initiatives, ensuring benefits for all. Chinese Vice President Han Zheng stated this at a UN meeting, emphasizing that these initiatives address the needs of the Global South and have transitioned from concepts to international actions.

item.title: Serbian President Resigns, Paving Way for Early Elections
item.description: Serbian President Aleksandar Vučić has resigned, opening the path for early presidential elections. He will not run again, having served two terms. Parliament Speaker Ana Brnabić will assume presidential duties temporarily. Vučić may seek the prime minister position.

item.title: Uzbekistan's representative addresses UN General Assembly, highlighting regional cooperation
item.description: Saida Mirziyoyeva, head of the Presidential Administration of Uzbekistan, spoke at the 81st UN General Assembly session. Her address focused on openness, dialogue, and cooperation, presenting Uzbekistan's stance on international security, UN reform, regional issues, Afghanistan, ecology, AI, and human capital. The speech emphasized the new dynamics in Central Asia and Uzbekistan's active role in shaping the regional agenda.

item.title: Uzbekistan Chess Team Wins 46th World Chess Olympiad
item.description: The Uzbekistan national chess team has achieved a historic victory at the 46th World Chess Olympiad. The team, comprising talented players and coaches, secured the title of two-time Olympiad champions. They demonstrated exceptional intellect, willpower, skill, and courage against strong international competition.

item.title: Kazakhstan Tops World Kickboxing Championship in Italy
item.description: The Kazakhstan national kickboxing team secured first place in the overall medal standings at the World Kickboxing Championship for juniors and youth in Lido di Jesolo, Italy. Kazakh kickboxers won a total of 66 medals, including 25 gold, 20 silver, and 21 bronze, across various disciplines and age categories.

item.title: Turkmenistan awards military personnel with high state honors and new military ranks
item.description: In recognition of their contributions to national defense and maintaining law and order, and marking the 35th anniversary of Independence, Turkmenistan's President Serdar Berdimuhamedow has signed decrees awarding military and law enforcement personnel with special ranks and professional qualifications. These honors recognize exemplary service and significant achievements in strengthening the nation's defense capabilities and ensuring public order.

item.title: US and Russia Remove Key Clause on Autonomous Weapons from Draft Agreement
item.description: The United States and Russia have removed a significant clause concerning autonomous weapons from a draft agreement. Negotiations for the agreement, which could have set rules for the use of lethal autonomous weapons, took place in early September at the UN in Switzerland.

item.title: Uruzgan residents report stalled construction of Aghajan Dam two years after groundbreaking
item.description: Residents of Uruzgan province state that construction of the Aghajan Dam, promised to irrigate over 100,000 hectares, has not begun two years after its groundbreaking ceremony. The dam was intended to have a storage capacity of over 70 million cubic meters. Local residents express concern over worsening drought conditions and the impact on their livelihoods.

item.title: Uzbekistan's tourism sector sees significant growth, with foreign tourist numbers increasing sixfold
item.description: Uzbekistan's tourism sector is experiencing significant growth, contributing to job creation and economic well-being. The country has seen a sixfold increase in foreign tourists since 2016, reaching nearly 12 million in 2025. Tourism service exports grew elevenfold to $4.8 billion. Uzbekistan was recognized as one of the world's fastest-growing tourist destinations.

item.title: Afghan citizens report increasing Taliban restrictions on religious freedom and ceremonies
item.description: Afghan citizens are reporting growing restrictions on religious freedom since the Taliban's takeover, affecting the observance of ceremonies and rites. Followers of Shia, Ismaili, and Sunni faiths are calling for respect for religious freedom, emphasizing that it includes the free performance of religious activities. They warn that continued restrictions could harm interfaith coexistence and religious diversity.
